acceptanceCriteria: authenticated-wake-delivery.md's Maturity line no longer says 0.1.0 or restricted npm. It describes Event Kit as publicly published, prerelease 2.x with Node 26+, without hard-coding a patch version that will drift. It keeps the non-qualification caveats.

The Maturity line and the upstream cross-references name D-006 and D-007 with their current status. The skill briefly states that every wake, filter, subscription and receiver route binds an explicit deliveryMode ('best-effort' | 'durable').
The Packages table lists the current published event-kit packages (adding provider and cli at minimum) or links to event-kit's AGENTS.md package list.
statement-graph.md 'Used by' either drops Immortalizer or marks it as pinned to a legacy (claim.v1/revoke.v1, schemas ~0.2.5) fold.

statement-graph.md (and, by cross-link, payload-schema-evolution.md) gives one explicit, sanctioned approach for revising a claimed vocabulary object's structure or meaning without `$version` or a `.vN` suffix. It also says how views and lexicons select semantics, consistent with the xl1-statement-graph WHITEPAPER wording.
authenticated-wake-delivery.md:62 links to that revision guidance for grant and revocation objects.
description:
Three follow-ups to the Layer 5 xl1-patterns Statement Graph rewrite in PR #107 (branch feature/statement-graph-fold4). That PR deliberately left them out. Line numbers below are for the PR branch; main and develop carry the same text unless noted. Found during the xl1-statement-graph 2026-10-06 code review follow-up.

1. Event Kit maturity is stale: skills/xl1-patterns/authenticated-wake-delivery.md:12 and :122
- Line 12 says "`@xyo-network/event-kit-*` **0.1.0** is published, restricted npm" and "D-002 through D-005 are accepted". Line 122 lists only D-002..D-005 as upstream decisions.
- Current Event Kit (XYOracleNetwork/event-kit main):
  - every package is 2.2.0 with `publishConfig.access: public`, LGPL-3.0-only and `engines.node >=26`, and npm `latest` is 2.2.0;
  - docs/decisions now has D-006 "Source-aware wake delivery" (accepted implementation direction, qualification gates remain) and D-007 "Explicit Best Effort and Durable delivery modes" (selected contract, release and hosted gates remain);
  - the wake envelope now requires `deliveryMode` ('best-effort' | 'durable'), `source`, `fromPosition`/`toPosition` and `filterHash` (packages/schemas/src/wakeEnvelope.ts:18-29).
- The Packages table (lines 68-79) omits `event-kit-provider`, `event-kit-cli`, `event-kit-vitest-config` and `event-kit-example`.
- The grant and revocation table (lines 57-58) is still accurate.
- Why it matters: the file is vendored into many XYOracleNetwork repos. An agent reading it will treat Event Kit as a restricted 0.1 prototype and will not know about delivery modes or source-aware wakes.

2. statement-graph.md:13 "Used by" lists Immortalizer
- Immortalizer pins `@xyo-network/xl1-statement-graph-schemas ~0.2.5` (packages/protocol/package.json:27).
- It imports the legacy `ClaimSchema`/`RevokeSchema` two-verb grammar (packages/protocol/src/replay.ts:4). Its conformance fixtures use `network.xyo.statement.claim.v1` and `revoke.v1`.
- Its README says the pilot performs no Statement Graph publication.
- The other listed users (LifeHash, Webble, Edge Node, Event Kit) are on 0.5.x.
- Listing Immortalizer points agents at a pre-subject, claim/revoke-era consumer. That contradicts the skill's own anti-pattern row against dual-reading `claim.v1`/`revoke.v1`.
- Fix: remove it, or mark it explicitly as on a legacy fold until it upgrades.

3. No guidance on revising a claimed vocabulary object
- statement-graph.md:48 says objects claimed through Statement Graph cannot carry `$` client metadata. The SG SDK writer throws on them. The section says not to plan a vocabulary revision around `$version`, but it gives no alternative.
- skills/xyo-knowledge/payload-schema-evolution.md:17-19 forbids structural `.vN` suffixes and says the structure revision belongs in `$version`.
- authenticated-wake-delivery.md:62 repeats the restriction for Event Kit grant and revocation objects.
- The Statement Graph white paper (WHITEPAPER.md:31, :574, :772, :847) says broader meaning requires "a new statement-object schema version", without saying how that version is expressed.
- Taken together, the skills leave a product author with no sanctioned way to evolve a claimed object's structure or meaning. An agent is likely to reach for a `.v2` suffix or for `$version`, and both are wrong.
- Fix: document the supported approach. Candidates:
  - a new descriptive schema name for a new kind;
  - a data-hash-bound body field when the revision must be authenticated;
  - additive changes only where the closure policy allows;
  - or say plainly that no in-place revision exists until the SG data-hash contract changes.
- Also say how views and lexicons select semantics. They pin lexicon documents per schema, and they never let an unbound field choose weaker rules.

Dependencies: land these after PR #107 merges, or as a follow-up commit on that branch. Item 3 should match whatever rule the xl1-statement-graph maintainers adopt for vocabulary versioning. It does not depend on any xl1-statement-graph package release. After the owner releases xyo-skills, consumers re-pin with `pnpm xy skills update`.
title: Fix stale Event Kit maturity and SG 'Used by'; add guidance for revising claimed objects
verification: git grep -n -E '0\.1\.0|restricted npm|D-002 through D-005' -- skills/xl1-patterns/authenticated-wake-delivery.md returns nothing
git grep -n -i immortalizer -- skills/xl1-patterns/statement-graph.md returns nothing, or only a line that marks it legacy
Read statement-graph.md's Existing hash contract section and confirm it names a positive revision approach and links from payload-schema-evolution.md's protocol-exceptions section
